cues.title: Lantern Thirty-Seven
cues.subtitle: Campaign 1: The Lantern Road  -  Level 1  -  3 Emberfall 1047 AK
cues.text: Brindle Cross is a crossroads village on the southern edge of the Lanternmarch, where the oldest lantern road in the Vael begins. Its lanterns have burned every night for three hundred years. Tonight four strangers share its market square at dusk: a soldier carrying dispatches, a Lamplighter archivist, a card player with a borrowed name, and the shrine's young acolyte. None of them knows the others yet.
Brindle Cross  -  Cards by the Well  -  Dusk
Again. Double or nothing, Mistress Mossfoot.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: Tam, please. 'Mistress' makes me sound like I own a boot shop.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: I've watched your hands the whole time. You can't cheat if I'm watching.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: Cheat? Me? I once beat a river captain using nothing but my honest face.
cues.speaker: tamsin

roll.purpose: c1: Palm the Crown card while Wil, who has lost three hands in a row, watches her fingers.

cues.text: The Crown card leaves Tamsin's sleeve and arrives in her hand. Wil, watching very closely, sees nothing at all.
Lantern and Crown. That's the hand, I'm afraid.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Eight blind! That was my honey-cake money.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: ...Here. Have a honey cake. Don't tell anyone I'm soft.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: A soldier's riding through tonight. Fort Harrow colours. I'm going to ask him to take me with him.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: A soldier. Lovely. I'll be sure to be somewhere else.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Brindle Cross  -  The Lantern Ledger  -  Dusk
Two candles already, and the night's barely started. Who's paying for those, the Eight?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: The Order of Lamplighters, Mistress Fenn. I will sign for them. I always sign for things.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

roll.purpose: c2: Spot what is wrong in a year of tidy entries for the lanterns south of the village.

cues.text: Here. Lantern thirty-seven, trimmed on the twenty-second of Harvestmoon. And again on the first of Emberfall.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: A lantern is trimmed once a year. And that mark is no warden's I know. I know all of them.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Is that bad? You've got the face my Wil makes before he tells me he's broken something.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: It is... irregular. I wrote it down.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Brindle Cross  -  The Dusk Devotion  -  Dusk
Hold the light. Hold the road. Hold on to each other.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Very good. Better than me; I always rush the middle part. Here, child. Hold out your hand.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: My sun-disc. Forty years round my neck. It's done more praying than I have.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Father, I can't take this. It's yours.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: The open hand holds more than the fist. Take it. My knees have earned the rest.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: A dwarf in a soldier's coat comes up the east road. He stops at the alms box, drops a coin, and says nothing.
You're the one who leaves silver and never stays for the hymn.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Didn't think anyone noticed.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: I count the box every night. Silver doesn't come often. What's your name?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Brannoc. Dispatches for Fort Harrow. Gone by morning.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Oriel. Light on your road, Brannoc.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: And on yours.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: The brass button on Oriel's collar catches the last of the sun. Father Tobin looks at it a moment too long.
Brindle Cross  -  Lantern Thirty-Seven  -  Dusk
Sir! You're from Fort Harrow? I can carry a pike. I've practised with a broom.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: Go home, lad. Your mother's looking for you.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Listen to the Big Man, Sprout. He's got a face like a locked door.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: And you are?
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Tam Mossfoot. Card player, storyteller, honest woman.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: She won every hand the boy played at the well. Every one. Statistically, that is remarkable.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Professor! You were counting my cards from across the square? I'm flattered.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Everyone's welcome in the square. Even card players. What's your name? Your real one?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: That was my real one, Sunshine. Cross my heart.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: On the south road, Lantern Thirty-Seven gutters once. Then the road is dark.
Did you feel that? Like a candle going out in my chest.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: A lantern cannot simply go out. That one has burned for three hundred years.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Quiet. Something on the road.
cues.speaker: brannoc

roll.purpose: c3: Make out shapes moving on the unlit south road before they reach the square.

cues.text: Brannoc stares into the dark and sees only dark. By the time the shapes have edges, they are already running.
Goblins! Mam! MAM!
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: Four goblins. One road. One of me. Fine. Get behind the shield.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: The goblins are fast and they are hungry, and they have already picked the one in the robes.
Brannoc's first swing ends the first goblin. He does not look at it twice.
The second dagger finds its mark. Ilsevel folds into the dust without a sound.
Tamsin's arrow takes the last runt in the shoulder. He drops, still breathing.
Brindle Cross  -  The One Left Breathing  -  Evening
Then it is quiet. Three goblins will not get up. The fourth is breathing. So, barely, is Ilsevel.
Ilsevel! Stay with me. Aurelan, if you're listening, now would be good.
cues.speaker: oriel

roll.purpose: a1: Healing Word on Ilsevel Starwick after the fight

cues.text: Warm light runs from Oriel's hands into Ilsevel like water into dry ground. Ilsevel's eyes open.
I am... technically fine. I would like it recorded that I was stabbed. Twice.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Recorded, Professor. Very brave. Mostly with your face.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: This one's alive. Small. Tie him up. Someone will want to ask him questions.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Do goblins carry coin? Asking for the village. Purely civic interest.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: He's bleeding. Hold the lamp closer, Brannoc. Nobody dies in my square tonight.
cues.speaker: oriel

roll.purpose: c4: Stop the bleeding of the goblin left alive, by lamplight, with her hands still shaking.

cues.text: Oriel's hands are shaking, and the bandage slips twice. The goblin lives, but only just. He won't be talking before morning.
Is it over? Who's hurt? Inside, the lot of you. There's stew on, and nobody argues with me tonight.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: You stood in front of all of us. You didn't even know our names.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: You kept them standing behind me. That's holding the line.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Then we held it together.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: ...Aye.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Free stew, then? Lovely. I'll bring the cards.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Next time: The goblin who talked.
